newsitem.title: USA: Senator says Los Angeles mayor diverted airport funds.
newsitem.headline: Senator says Los Angeles mayor diverted airport funds.

text.p: A senator charged Monday that Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan diverted more than $31 million in federal airport funds hours before Congress voted to bar such moves by localities.

Sen. John McCain, R-Ariz., said in a two-page letter to Riordan that the mayor improperly diverted U.S. funds targeted for Los Angeles International Airport to pay city police and firefighters and other bills.
McCain said if Los Angeles did not return the $31 million, he would push to have the city's federal airport funding slashed by that amount.
Riordan's office had no immediate response, but another city official defended the move.

"The middle-of-the-night scheme" blatantly "circumvents" the spirit of a federal aviation bill approved by Congress on Oct. 3, McCain, chairman of the aviation subpanel of the Senate Commerce Committee, said in the letter.
"The city's action will not fool anyone," McCain said, adding he will ask Secretary of Transportation Federico Pena to "use all authority he has" to resolve the situation.
Los Angeles City Controller Rick Tuttle said he would stand by his decision to transfer the $31 million from the airport to the city's general fund.

"These are monies that are owed to the taxpayers of the city," Tuttle said. "Efforts to link it to other appropriations or to future airport funding is inappropriate. It's money we're owed and entitled to."

Tuttle maintains the $31 million was repayment for past investments by the city in the airport. The investments were for fire safety and certain public works projects. Tuttle said the city's attorneys had approved the legality of the move.
"To make these threats (is) inappropriate," Tuttle said. "As far as using the money and moving forward, that's my view. We should move forward."
John Driscoll, executive director of the Los Angeles Department of Airports, also defended the fund transfer.

"Under the eyes of our city attorney, it was determined to be a legal transfer," said Driscoll. "But independent of legal advise, they (the Los Angeles City Council) can still say they're not going to take that money. They can send it back."
Title 8 of the airport bill passed by Congress, and which President Clinton is expected to sign this week, strengthens federal laws that bar municipalities from diverting federal airport dollars.
Under the bill, the Federal Aviation Reauthorization Act of 1996, cities can ask the federal government to reimburse them for contributions they have made to airports for the past six years.
Riordan contends the federal government owes Los Angeles millions of dollars for city purchases of airport land dating back 70 years ago, McCain's office said.
